cards.title: The 5 words behind every great photograph
cards.takeaway: Whether shot on a smartphone or a pro camera, a strong photo nails five things: Clarity, Light, Composition, Moment, and Purpose.
cards.body:
Expensive gear never rescues bad light or a blurry hand! Every memorable photograph combines **five qualities**:
1. **Clarity:** The main subject is crisp and sharp.
2. **Light:** Bright enough to see clean detail without harsh washout.
3. **Composition:** Thoughtful framing — nothing distracting photobombs the edges.
4. **Moment:** Captured at the right expression or action.
5. **Purpose:** Fits its job (WhatsApp product catalog, portrait, event).

cards.title: Light direction — why standing in front of a bright window turns faces dark!
cards.takeaway: Face your subject TOWARD the window or soft light — putting a bright window BEHIND them tricks the camera into turning them into a dark shadow!
cards.body:
Have you ever snapped someone standing **in front of a bright window** and their face came out pitch-black?

- **Why it happens (Backlighting):** The camera sees the super-bright window behind them and darkens the whole shot so the window doesn't glow white — leaving your subject's face in shadow!
- **Instant fix:** Turn around so **you** have your back to the window and the soft window light falls **onto** your subject's face (or product handbag)!

check.prompt: You photograph a friend standing with a bright sunny window right BEHIND her, and her face comes out dark and almost invisible. Why?

choices.text: The camera exposed for the bright background window (backlighting), underexposing her face — turn so the window light faces her!
Phone cameras cannot photograph people indoors

check.hint: Put the light source in FRONT of (or 45° beside) your subject, not blazing right behind them!
check.explanation: Spot on! Strong backlighting fools automatic exposure — turning your subject to face the window gives flattering, clear light immediately.

cards.title: The Exposure Triangle — Aperture, Shutter Speed & ISO
cards.takeaway: Aperture = how wide the lens opens, Shutter Speed = how long light enters, and ISO = how sensitive the sensor is to light.
cards.body:
Three controls balance brightness (**exposure**) and look:
- **Aperture (`f/1.8`, `f/8`):** **How wide the lens opens** (wide opening lets in more light and blurs the background softly).
- **Shutter Speed (`1/500s`, `1/30s`):** **How long the shutter stays open** (fast freezes motion; too slow causes motion blur).
- **ISO (`100`, `3200`):** **How sensitive the digital sensor is** (low ISO = clean & smooth; sky-high ISO in the dark adds grainy 'noise'!).

check.prompt: In the Exposure Triangle, what do Aperture, Shutter Speed, and ISO control?

choices.text: Aperture = how wide the lens opens, Shutter Speed = how long light enters, ISO = sensor light sensitivity
Aperture = battery life, Shutter Speed = zoom distance, ISO = Wi-Fi speed
All three only add colour filters
Aperture = speaker volume, Shutter Speed = file name, ISO = folder path

check.hint: Opening width (Aperture), time open (Shutter Speed), sensor boost (ISO)!
check.explanation: Nailed it! Balancing Aperture, Shutter Speed, and ISO gives you full control over brightness, sharpness, and grain.

cards.title: Fixing blurry or too-dark WhatsApp product photos
cards.takeaway: Clean your lens first, steady your hands + use faster shutter/better light for blur, and move products near soft daylight instead of dark corners.
cards.body:
Two everyday fixes every creator uses daily:
1. **Whole photo looks smeared/blurry?** Either **camera shake** (hands moved during a slow shutter speed — brace your elbows or add more light!) or **missed focus** (tap the subject on screen and wipe finger grease off the lens!).
2. **Handbag looks sharp yet too dark for WhatsApp Business?** Move the bag next to an open window / shaded doorway in natural daylight and bounce light onto the shadow side with a plain white cardboard sheet!

check.prompt: What are the FIVE quality words this course uses to judge whether a photograph works well?

choices.text: Clarity, Light, Composition, Moment, and Purpose
Price, Brand, Megapixels, Tripod, and Flash
Red, Green, Blue, Black, and White
Zoom, Crop, Filter, Sticker, and Caption

check.hint: Sharpness (Clarity), illumination (Light), framing (Composition), timing (Moment), and job (Purpose).
check.explanation: 100% right! Clarity, Light, Composition, Moment, and Purpose work together on every camera from an Android phone to a cinema rig.
